title: crypto2dev_setkey ECC_PRIV: closes old devCtx before new import succeeds — window of no key
description: In crypto2dev_setkey() for WC_SETKEY_ECC_PRIV and WC_SETKEY_ECC_PUB: on the error path ('if (new_fd < 0)'), the code closes the existing devCtx fd and sets it to NULL before returning the error code. This is wrong. If crypto2dev_key_import() fails (e.g., ENOENT because the device temporarily has no ECDSA provider), the old working key fd is destroyed and the key object is left with devCtx=NULL. Any subsequent sign/verify on the same ecc_key object hits 'devCtx == NULL → CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE' — the key silently falls to software, but the ecc_key itself may have no software-usable private key bytes loaded (e.g., if the caller only imported a raw scalar into the port and relied on the KEY fd). Trigger: re-keying fails transiently; old key is gone, new key was never installed.
